parts.title: The Letter
parts.text: A lawyer's letter changed Beatrix's spring break. Her great-aunt Odalys had died, and Beatrix and her cousin Julian were to **inherit** Ravenscroft **manor**, a gray stone house on the moors. Their neighbor Anaya, a gifted puzzle-solver, came along. Nobody in the family had visited in years, because Odalys had grown **reclusive**, shutting her gates to visitors and rarely stepping outside.

parts.title: The Portrait
parts.text: In the **parlor**, a portrait showed an **aristocrat** in a velvet coat, an ancestor who had once ruled the county's high society. The house still reflected his **decadent** tastes: gilded mirrors, a ceiling crowded with painted cherubs, and a dining table set for forty. Julian shrugged at the **ostentatious** display of wealth. "This place was built to impress people," he muttered.

parts.title: The Riddle
parts.text: Anaya noticed that the portrait hung slightly crooked. Behind it was a folded note with a **cryptic** message: "The truth sleeps where the clock forgets to tick." It was an **enigma** they could not put down. They found a stopped grandfather clock in the library, and inside its base lay a hidden drawer of ledgers. Odalys had run a **clandestine** scholarship fund for decades, paying school fees for local children while the family assumed she hoarded her money. When Mr. Pell, the lawyer, arrived that evening and saw the open drawer, he gave a **furtive** glance toward the door, as if guarding a secret. Years earlier, a **scandal** had cracked the family's name: a newspaper rumor that Odalys had stolen from the estate.

parts.title: The Truth
parts.text: The cousins decided to keep the fund running, and Mr. Pell confirmed that Odalys had refused to correct the rumor. Beatrix thought about how easily a rumor can harden into fact. The quietest person in the family had been its most generous, and the proof had been hiding behind a crooked frame all along.

definitions.meaning1: A large country house with land around it, often the home of a wealthy family. Example: The old manor sat at the end of a long, tree-lined road.
definitions.meaning2: In the past, the land and village controlled by a lord. Example: Farmers on the medieval manor paid rent to the lord in grain.
definitions.studentChallenge: The family lived in a stately ___ surrounded by acres of gardens and woods.

definitions.meaning1: A person, thing or situation that is mysterious and hard to understand. Example: The missing painting remained an enigma to the detectives.
definitions.studentChallenge: Nobody could explain why the lighthouse lamp turned on by itself; it was a true ___.

definitions.meaning1: Done in secret, usually because it is forbidden or meant to be hidden. Example: The rebels held clandestine meetings in a cellar.
definitions.studentChallenge: The friends planned a ___ surprise party and told no one.

definitions.meaning1: Preferring to live alone and avoid other people. Example: The reclusive author never gave interviews.
definitions.studentChallenge: Her ___ neighbor rarely left the house and never came to the block party.

definitions.meaning1: Marked by luxury and indulgence, often to an excessive degree. Example: The decadent banquet had seven courses and a chocolate fountain.
definitions.meaning2: In a state of moral or cultural decline. Example: Historians described the empire in its final years as decadent.
definitions.studentChallenge: After the long hike, we treated ourselves to a ___ triple-layer chocolate cake.

definitions.meaning1: A member of the highest social class, usually with inherited wealth or a title. Example: The aristocrat arrived at the ball in a horse-drawn carriage.
definitions.studentChallenge: In the old kingdom, an ___ owned land simply because of his family's title.

definitions.meaning1: Showy in a way meant to impress others, especially with wealth. Example: His ostentatious gold watch flashed every time he reached for the menu.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ mansion had fountains in the driveway and a statue of the owner.

definitions.meaning1: Done in a secretive, sneaky way to avoid being noticed. Example: He cast a furtive glance at the clock and slipped out the back door.
definitions.studentChallenge: The cat gave a ___ look around before sneaking onto the kitchen counter.

definitions.meaning1: Having a hidden or puzzling meaning that is hard to understand. Example: The fortune cookie held a cryptic message about rivers and doors.
definitions.studentChallenge: Her ___ reply left us more confused than before.

definitions.meaning1: To receive money, property or a title from someone who has died. Example: She will inherit her grandmother's violin.
definitions.meaning2: To receive a trait from a parent through genes. Example: Many people inherit their curly hair from a parent.
definitions.studentChallenge: When her uncle died, she was surprised to ___ his entire stamp collection.

definitions.meaning1: A room in a house for receiving guests and conversation. Example: Guests waited in the parlor while tea was prepared.
definitions.meaning2: A shop that offers a certain service or product. Example: The ice cream parlor was crowded on summer evenings.
definitions.studentChallenge: We sat in the front ___ and chatted with our hosts before dinner.

definitions.meaning1: An event that shocks the public and damages a reputation, often involving wrongdoing. Example: The mayor resigned after the scandal over missing funds.
definitions.meaning2: Harmful gossip about other people. Example: The town loved scandal and talked of little else.
definitions.studentChallenge: The politician's career ended after the ___ was exposed in the newspaper.
